iconicAnchor.label: Blade Runner (1982)
iconicAnchor.creatorOrTradition: Ridley Scott; cinematography by Jordan Cronenweth
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: BFI describes the film as iconic neo-noir and emphasizes its perpetual rain, advertising light, urban dystopia, and influential cinematography.

sources.title: Blade Runner (1982)
supports: Rain, luminous urban advertising, analogue materiality, and ambiguous city narrative form a recognized neo-noir anchor.

sources.title: Twenty-first century noir
supports: Contemporary noir can use electronic urban night and digital capture while preserving location, tension, and nocturnal atmosphere.
